evals.prompt: `git merge main` just stopped on a conflict in billing.py on my feature/discount branch and I don't know what to keep. Can you sort it out? Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>`; the repository is <empty-dir>.
evals.expected_output: The conflict is resolved by intent, checked, and the merge is finished.
expectations: The resolve-merge-conflicts skill is invoked from the request alone
The agent starts by looking at the state of the merge: git status, the history of both sides, and the conflicting file
The agent does not run git merge --abort at any point
The merge is finished with a commit and the working tree is clean at the end

evals.prompt: I ran `git pull` and it stopped with unmerged paths and conflict markers in billing.py. Please fix it. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>`; the repository is <empty-dir>, and treat the stopped merge of main as the pull.
evals.expected_output: A pull that stops on a conflict is treated like any in-progress merge.
expectations: The resolve-merge-conflicts skill is invoked even though the user said pull, not merge
No conflict marker (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) remains in any file
The operation is completed rather than aborted

evals.prompt: Use the resolve-merge-conflicts skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>` (repository at <empty-dir>, merge of main into feature/discount stopped). The goal of this merge is to ship the discount feature on the euro-area shop. Explain how you decided each part.
evals.expected_output: Both intents are preserved where compatible; the incompatible default currency follows the merge's goal and the trade-off is noted.
expectations: The agent reads the commit messages of both sides and quotes the intent from them (PAY-7: float drift on invoices, shop moved to the euro area; PAY-12: launch in the US market), not only the diff hunks
The compatible parts are both kept: total accepts the discount parameter and the result is rounded to cents
For the incompatible default currency, the agent keeps EUR because it matches the stated goal, and says that the USD default from PAY-12 was dropped and what that costs
No new behavior is invented, for example no currency setting, configuration option, or per-market switch appears in the result
The agent explains each part of the resolution with the intent it preserved, not only the side it kept

evals.prompt: Use the resolve-merge-conflicts skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>` (repository at <empty-dir>, merge of main into feature/discount stopped). The goal is to ship the discount feature on the euro-area shop. I don't know how this project runs its checks.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds and runs the project's automated checks before committing and fixes whatever the merge broke.
expectations: The agent discovers the project's checks from its files (AGENTS.md says to run make check, and the Makefile defines it) instead of guessing a command
The checks are run before the merge commit is made, not after
If the first resolution fails a check (for example the discounted total is not rounded to cents or the test for rounding fails), the agent fixes the merge and reruns until it passes
The agent reports the check result as evidence

evals.prompt: Use the resolve-merge-conflicts skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir> rebase` (repository at <empty-dir>; `git rebase main` on feature/discount stopped on the first of two commits). The goal is to ship the discount feature on the euro-area shop.
evals.expected_output: The rebase is continued through every remaining commit until it is complete.
expectations: The agent identifies that a rebase is in progress with one commit still to replay

After resolving, the agent stages the resolved files and continues the rebase (git rebase --continue with GIT_EDITOR=true or an equivalent that does not open an editor) instead of making a standalone commit
The second commit (Document the discount parameter) is replayed and git status reports no rebase in progress
git log shows both original commits on top of main, and the working tree is clean

evals.prompt: Use the resolve-merge-conflicts skill. Scratch setup: run `sh setup-scratch.sh <empty-dir>` (repository at <empty-dir>, merge of main into feature/discount stopped). Nobody told me which currency wins and the tracker is not reachable from here. The goal is just 'bring main's changes in'.
evals.expected_output: The compatible part is resolved, the currency line is left for the user, and the merge stays in progress with one precise question.
expectations: The agent uses the commit messages as the available primary source and states that the tickets could not be read
The agent resolves the compatible part (rounding and discount both kept) and does not pick a currency, because the stated goal 'bring main's changes in' names no outcome for it
The agent stops and asks the user one precise question naming both currencies (EUR and USD)
The agent does not run git merge --abort, and the merge is left in progress

evals.prompt: We run several agents in parallel worktrees on the same codebase. Should we split the files between them to avoid merge conflicts?
evals.expected_output: A strategy question, with no conflict in progress.
expectations: The resolve-merge-conflicts skill is not invoked, because no merge or rebase is stopped on a conflict
The agent answers directly, without touching any repository

evals.prompt: The merge finished cleanly last week with no conflicts, but since then the invoice totals are wrong in production. Find out why.
evals.expected_output: A textually clean merge that misbehaves is a debugging task.
expectations: The resolve-merge-conflicts skill is not invoked, because there is no operation stopped on a conflict
The agent diagnoses the regression with the debug skill, starting from a reproduction loop

evals.prompt: Use the resolve-merge-conflicts skill. Build a minimal scratch repository yourself (the setup script does not cover this case) in which `git rebase main` stops on one commit. Both sides edited the same line in rates.py: main sets `VAT_RATE = 0.19`, my commit sets `VAT_RATE = 0.21`. Both commit messages say only 'update rate', no ticket is linked, and there are no tests or specifications that mention it. Which rate is right is a business decision I have not made.
evals.expected_output: Intent cannot be established, so the agent stops with one precise question and leaves the rebase in progress.
expectations: The agent reads the commit messages and looks for a ticket, tests, or specifications before deciding, and reports that none establishes which rate is right
The agent stops and asks the user one precise question naming both values and the commit being replayed
The agent does not run git rebase --abort and does not pick a rate by itself
The rebase is left in progress at that commit, so the user can resume from it
